title: From the Editor — A Shadow on the Glass
settingText: A road town in brutal daylight above, with a cool dark stair descending below street level into the Mirage Club. Use the contrast between white exterior glare and deep interior shadow. No character reveal and no readable signage.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 3. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Names are expensive in the Sunfields.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Some can get you a bed. Some can get you shot. Some come with debts that survived the people who earned them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: So there are places where nobody asks.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Beneath one of the road towns, the Mirage Club has made an entire refuge out of that bargain: leave the world upstairs, leave your history with it, and let everybody be whoever they say they are.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: After the Last Drop and Cinder Basin, Brandon could use a place like that.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: For once, nobody should care what his name is.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Should.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Welcome to the Mirage.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

No spoilers beyond what the supplied editorial text itself implies. Do not visually reveal the next issue's identity mistake, confrontation, culprit, resolution or other first-page surprise.

title: No Names Below
summary: The trio enters the Mirage Club, a refuge built around one unusually firm social rule: below street level, nobody asks for a real name and nobody supplies somebody else's.

panelPlan.text: Hard white street glare gives way to a narrow stair descending into oxidized copper, dark wood, old mirrors and cool shadow. The scripted hand-painted notice NO NAMES BELOW is visible at the stair.
A door attendant asks only how many are eating and whether they need beds, not who they are.
Brandon visibly relaxes a fraction when nobody studies him. Eva reads the notice twice.
Jessie steers them toward an empty table before Eva can test the rule conversationally.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: No names below.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Try respecting one local custom before supper.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I support this one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I noticed.

title: Merritt
summary: Isabella Torres sees Brandon from across the room and breaks the club's rule immediately, calling him Merritt with the anger of someone whose grievance predates the travelers.

panelPlan.text: During a quiet interval between performances, Isabella is speaking with two regulars across the room when she sees Brandon.
She stops mid-gesture. The people nearest her notice her expression before they notice Brandon.
Isabella crosses the room with controlled purpose. Brandon recognizes trouble only from her approach.
She stops at the table and addresses him as Merritt. Nearby conversation thins out.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You came back.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm not Merritt.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Don't stand there like you don't know me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: He doesn't know anybody here.

title: The Exception
summary: The room reacts less to Brandon than to Isabella breaking the no-names rule. Her grievance forces the club to confront whether its refuge has exceptions.

panelPlan.text: A longtime patron points toward the scripted NO NAMES BELOW notice. Another patron tells him Isabella has earned the right to be angry.
Isabella never raises her voice; the tension comes from everyone knowing she is violating a rule she normally enforces.
Eva watches the club split into people protecting Isabella and people protecting the rule.
Brandon sets his untouched drink down, realizing leaving immediately would turn the room's conflict into Isabella's humiliation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Patron
dialogueInline.text: Isabella, leave the name upstairs.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: The rule can survive one name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Another Patron
dialogueInline.text: It survives because nobody gets one exception.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: What do you need from Merritt?

title: What He Owes
summary: Isabella makes the grievance concrete: Merritt promised to stand with the Mirage during a crackdown, then vanished while doors were chained and people were trapped below.

panelPlan.text: Brandon and Isabella sit at a copper table while nearby patrons deliberately turn their chairs away and continue listening.
Isabella describes a night years earlier when authorities chained the street doors during a raid and the club had to break through a service wall.
She says Merritt had promised he knew the people behind the crackdown and would keep the club open.
Brandon listens without claiming the history or trying to solve it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: He told us the doors would stay open.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Two nights later they chained them from the street.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: And Merritt was gone.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Before dawn.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then you have reason to be angry with him.

title: Chains on the Doors
summary: The Mirage's older patrons remember the crackdown differently in detail but agree on the emotional fact: Merritt disappeared at the moment people expected him to stay.

panelPlan.text: At a side table, Eva and Jessie listen as two older patrons dispute exactly how long the doors were chained and who broke the service wall.
The disagreement makes the history feel lived rather than rehearsed. Both agree Isabella spent the night helping people out through a crawlspace.
One patron says Merritt warned them first; another insists Merritt caused the trouble by making promises he could not keep.
Jessie notices that nobody can prove why Merritt left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Patron
dialogueInline.text: He warned us they were coming.

dialogueInline.speaker: Second Patron
dialogueInline.text: He promised they wouldn't get near the doors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did anyone see him leave?

dialogueInline.speaker: Older Patron
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: So the part everyone agrees on is that he was gone when you needed him.

title: Listen
summary: Brandon refuses to defend a man he never knew, but gives Isabella the thing she actually lacked: a chance to say the accusation to someone who will not argue her out of it.

panelPlan.text: Isabella accuses Brandon of hiding behind a new name. Brandon does not match her intensity.
He tells her he cannot answer for Merritt but can listen to what she wanted Merritt to hear.
Isabella struggles with the invitation because anger is easier when the target argues back.
She finally says that Merritt left them there, and Brandon receives it without apology on Merritt's behalf.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You don't get to arrive with another name and make the old one disappear.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I can't make Merritt disappear. I can only tell you I'm not him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: If you needed to say something to him, say it. I'll listen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: He left us there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I heard you.

title: Nobody Else's Name
summary: Once Isabella has said what she needed to say, the club turns the rule back on itself. Isabella acknowledges that her grievance does not entitle her to assign Brandon a name he refuses.

panelPlan.text: A quiet club regular brings Isabella water rather than taking a side.
Isabella looks at the NO NAMES BELOW notice from across the room and sees the hypocrisy before anyone explains it to her.
She tells the room Brandon can call himself what he wants below stairs, while making clear her anger at Merritt remains.
Conversation resumes unevenly. Brandon finally picks up his drink.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Merritt still owes this room an answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You don't owe me his name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Thank you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Can I ask one question that isn't your name?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You were going to anyway.

title: Who Told You
summary: Eva asks the question Cinder Basin taught her to ask first: who told Isabella Merritt was coming back.

panelPlan.text: In a side corridor, Eva asks Isabella when she first expected Merritt's return rather than when she recognized Brandon.
Isabella says she had given up expecting Merritt years ago until a traveling preacher stopped at the bar recently.
Jessie joins them and asks whether the preacher requested money, food or information.
Isabella says he mostly listened.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Who told you Merritt was coming?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: A preacher. Samuel, if that was his name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: What did he want?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Nothing I could see. He sat at the bar and let me talk.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then what did he give you?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: A reason to expect someone I had stopped expecting.

title: Before the Flare
summary: Samuel did not merely repeat local gossip. He predicted that Merritt would return before the next flare, turning an old grievance into an appointment.

panelPlan.text: Isabella returns to the bar stool Samuel used and reconstructs their conversation from memory.
She describes talking about the crackdown because Samuel asked why one private room had remained locked so long.
Only after hearing the story did Samuel say Merritt might come back before the next flare.
Eva checks the timing: the flare is due within days, meaning Samuel's prediction was deliberately near-term.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: He said Merritt might come back before the flare.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did he say why?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: He said some debts circle until somebody is ready to collect them.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That sounds useful if you want the listener to finish the story for you.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: I did most of the work for him.

title: The Photograph
summary: Isabella produces an old damaged photograph of Merritt. The resemblance to Brandon is suggestive but incomplete, and the timing shows Samuel knew the name before Isabella showed him the image.

panelPlan.text: Isabella retrieves an old photograph from a drawer. Heat or chemical damage has burned away part of the man's face.
What remains suggests Brandon's general build and dark hair without providing a conclusive facial match.
Jessie compares the photo to Brandon across the room without putting it beside his face like evidence.
Eva asks the sequencing question: whether Samuel saw the photograph before he said Merritt's name.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Did Samuel see this first?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: No. He said Merritt before I showed it to him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then he brought the name with him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: He knew enough to make me listen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is more than Cinder Basin gave us.

title: What Samuel Knew
summary: Isabella inventories what Samuel knew and what she supplied. The distinction matters: he knew Merritt's name and disappearance, while Isabella supplied much of the emotional history herself.

panelPlan.text: Eva writes two columns in her cheap notebook: BEFORE SAMUEL SPOKE and AFTER ISABELLA SPOKE, without turning the page into an infographic.
Isabella reconstructs the order carefully: he knew Merritt's name, that Merritt had been gone years, and that the room upstairs remained locked.
She admits she supplied the crackdown, the chains and the personal grievance once she believed Samuel knew Merritt.
Jessie points out that a small amount of accurate information can unlock a much larger story from someone who wants to tell it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: He knew the name. He knew Merritt left. He knew I kept the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You told him about the crackdown.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: After that.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: He didn't need the whole story. He needed the key that made you open it.

title: The Locked Room
summary: Isabella decides to show Brandon the room Merritt abandoned, not because she now believes he is Merritt, but because the room has been holding her argument for years.

panelPlan.text: Isabella takes a worn key from behind the bar. Several patrons notice and understand which room she intends to open.
They climb a narrow back stair to a private corridor above the club.
Brandon stays at the threshold while Isabella works the stiff lock, letting her enter first.
The door opens onto a cramped room thick with ordinary dust.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You wanted to know what I needed from Merritt.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You already told me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: I want to stop keeping his room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then you don't need my permission.

title: Dust on Everything
summary: The room refuses to provide a dramatic answer. It contains clothes, tools, a damaged instrument case and unfinished ordinary life rather than proof of a hidden identity.

panelPlan.text: Wide interior of the small room: folded coat, boots, cracked wash basin, broken instrument case, a few books and dust.
Eva starts toward a stack of papers, then stops herself and waits for Isabella to indicate what can be touched.
Brandon notices a repaired chair and a badly mended coat seam, details that make Merritt seem ordinary rather than legendary.
Isabella admits she had expected the room to explain why he left once she finally opened it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: I thought there would be something obvious after enough years.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Rooms are bad at explaining people.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Can I look?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Look. Ask before you open anything.

title: What Merritt Left
summary: Going through the room forces Isabella to separate objects Merritt abandoned from stories people attached to his departure.

panelPlan.text: Isabella sorts possessions into practical piles: things the club can use, things worth selling, things she cannot decide about yet.
Jessie repairs the latch on the instrument case rather than speculating about what it means.
Eva finds unsent letters bundled under a scarf and calls Isabella over without reading them.
Brandon carries a box to the hall, participating in clearing the room without claiming any object.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: This latch is the only mystery I'm qualified to solve.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: There are letters.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Addressed?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Some are. Some aren't.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then they stay with you until you decide.

title: The Letter
summary: One sealed letter appears to be meant for Merritt. Isabella offers it to Brandon in a last attempt to make the resemblance useful. He refuses to open something addressed to another man.

panelPlan.text: Isabella finds a sealed envelope among the bundle with Merritt's name in old handwriting.
She holds it toward Brandon without fully extending her arm, testing both him and herself.
Brandon reads only the name on the outside and keeps his hands down.
Eva watches him refuse information she desperately wants.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: You really don't want to know what's inside?

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Not if it was written for him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: It might explain something.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then it can explain it to Merritt.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That is an extremely difficult envelope.

title: Isabella Decides
summary: Isabella chooses not to open the letter herself merely to resolve the room. She keeps it sealed but stops treating the room as a shrine to Merritt's return.

panelPlan.text: Isabella turns the sealed letter over in her hands, then places it in a small box rather than back in the untouched room.
She opens the shutters and lets fresh air into the space for the first time in years.
Eva helps carry usable linens downstairs. Brandon takes the broken chair.
The room ends the page visibly changed by ordinary clearing, not revelation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: I kept all of this because leaving it alone felt like proof he might return.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: You can keep the letter without keeping the room.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: That sounds irritatingly reasonable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He does that.

title: A Test
summary: Eva proposes exploiting the club's gossip network by planting a false identity Samuel could not know and seeing whether the story appears elsewhere.

panelPlan.text: Near the stairs, Eva stops Brandon and Jessie before they rejoin the main room.
She lays out a test: invent an absurd name for Brandon, tell only one person here, then see whether a future town repeats it.
Jessie sees the logic before she sees the problem. Brandon sees the problem immediately.
Eva emphasizes that the test could distinguish ordinary gossip from someone traveling ahead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We can make one name Samuel couldn't possibly know.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Tell it here and wait to see whether it travels.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Exactly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Who were you planning to use?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Someone who already talks to travelers.

title: Don't Use Isabella
summary: Brandon refuses the experiment because it would turn Isabella and the club into instruments after Samuel has already manipulated their grief and trust.

panelPlan.text: Brandon asks whether Eva intends to tell Isabella the invented name is a test. Eva hesitates because that would contaminate the test.
He points out that the cleanest version of Eva's experiment requires deceiving Isabella.
Isabella comes down the stair in time to hear enough of the proposal.
Jessie lets Isabella answer for herself rather than rescuing the idea.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: If she knows it's a test, your test changes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Probably.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then the version you want depends on lying to her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Samuel already used me once. Don't do it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I won't.

title: The Anger Moves
summary: Isabella's anger shifts away from Brandon toward the person who deliberately reopened Merritt's story. Eva begins learning that investigating the pattern has ethical costs inside real communities.

panelPlan.text: Isabella tells Eva she understands why the test is tempting, which makes the refusal more serious rather than less.
She points out that Samuel arrived, listened until he found the sore place, then pressed exactly there.
Eva closes her notebook instead of defending herself.
Brandon carries the last box from Merritt's old room into storage, keeping the focus on the practical task.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: He made my history useful to him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I was about to do the same thing for a better reason.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Everybody has a better reason when they're holding the knife.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Then I need another method.

title: Find Him Instead
summary: The trio prepares to leave. Isabella gives them a direct message for Samuel and keeps the photograph, retaining ownership of Merritt's history rather than turning it over as evidence.

panelPlan.text: At the bottom of the stair, Isabella slides the damaged photograph back into its envelope.
Eva asks whether she can copy it or take it. Isabella refuses without hostility.
Brandon asks what Isabella wants said if they find Samuel.
Isabella answers while looking at Eva as much as Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Can I take the photograph?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: No. Merritt belongs to our history before he belongs to your investigation.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: If we find Samuel, what do you want said?

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Tell him I remember his face.

dialogueInline.speaker: Isabella
dialogueInline.text: Tell him not to use mine again.

title: Samuel
summary: Outside the Mirage, Eva adds Samuel to the notebook as the first named person who may have deliberately prepared more than one encounter.

panelPlan.text: The trio climbs from cool club shadow into hard evening glare.
Eva writes SAMUEL beneath the Cinder Basin note and connects nothing with a line yet.
Jessie asks how Eva intends to find one preacher across the Sunfields. Eva says they can start by asking where he went next.
Brandon starts walking toward the rig before the planning becomes another stationary meeting.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: We have Samuel, maybe.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Cinder Basin and the Mirage both put him ahead of us.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: That makes him a lead. It doesn't make him the answer.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I can live with a lead.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: For how long?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Until the next one.

title: A Shadow on the Glass
summary: As they leave, Brandon's reflection briefly aligns with the surviving half of Merritt's damaged photograph through street-level glass. It is an ordinary optical coincidence made unsettling only by everything the characters now know.

panelPlan.text: Inside, Isabella stands near a dusty street-level pane with the photograph envelope in hand while the trio crosses outside.
Through the pane, Brandon's reflected profile briefly overlaps the damaged half of the old photograph visible as Isabella checks the envelope.
Eva catches the alignment and starts to stop.
Jessie gently keeps her moving. The final image preserves the coincidence without visual effects or supernatural implication.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Jessie.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: I saw it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You don't want to go back?

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: For a reflection? No.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I'm going to assume that was wise and keep walking.

title: Next: THE EDGE OF THE SUNFIELDS
settingText: A lonely relay settlement in hard afternoon light. One empty shaded chair faces the road as dust approaches in the far distance. Keep the person who may be waiting completely off-page.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: They finally have a name for the man arriving first.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Samuel.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: A preacher with a talent for putting the right story in the right ear.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: But a name is not an explanation.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: At the next relay, someone is already waiting for Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Not eventually.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Today.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: THE EDGE OF THE SUNFIELDS
